scope: Read-only review of Root's final C4 bot-save and terminal-reward retry UI changes and six prepared widget cases.

dependencies_read.scope: Clock schedule/pause/resume/cancel and actual pause-panel actions.

exact_inverse.other_product_bytes: byte-identical to freshly read exact28462 source

original_concrete_risk_closed.finding: After awaiting a reward retry the intermediate method called _finish directly even if Home/Pause arrived during the await. A drawn result could open immediately; a winning result could start its presentation while paused.
original_concrete_risk_closed.final_change: The successful completion schedules a zero-delay callback through the existing paused clock. The callback revalidates current owner, round generation and native-opening state before _finish.
original_concrete_risk_closed.new_regression: Lifecycle pause during reward retry defers the settled result

findings: An uncommitted bot move is re-armed only for the still-current owner and UI round generation, while the round is playing, Lumo is next and local two-player mode is off.

_saveError pauses the clock first. Re-arming stores one pending action; there is no automatic retry until Fortsetzen resumes the clock. Restart/dispose cancel the old pending action and the callback checks generation/owner.
For an already committed terminal board the retry calls only the controller's existing settleReward; no column is dropped. Further failure pauses and stores another explicit retry.

The successful terminal reward path now delegates display to the same clock and checks identity again in the callback. A lifecycle pause during the write therefore preserves the pending display without repeating the confirmed reward.

The six prepared cases use the production widget/controller/AppState/learning storage, an explicit MissingPlugin fallback, real taps and a controlled platform write. They cover first bot retry, repeated failure, restart cancellation, local Gold, saved seven-piece win, and lifecycle pause during a held reward acknowledgement.

The held-wallet case releases a real pending backend response after AppLifecycleState.inactive, expects the five-star state with no result dialog, then requires another explicit Fortsetzen for the dialog. Board counts stay four child/three Lumo pieces.
limits: This static review does not establish compilation, a passed Flutter case, Android behavior or a rendered result.

The C4 fixture rejects writes before backend persistence. The separate Memory/native-optimistic-cache and Wallet-acknowledgement cases cover a different boundary; their claims are not transferred here.
Rules, persistence repository, queue, native session, other widget geometry and workflow gates were not changed by this patch or reviewer.
